meta_desc: StoryGraph or BookWorm? Deep stats and mood-based picks, or a calm daily habit with streaks, a reading timer, widgets and audiobooks in minutes.
h1: StoryGraph or BookWorm? It depends what you want from a tracker.
lede: StoryGraph is wonderful at looking back: charts, moods and recommendations. BookWorm is built for the day in front of you: today's pages, a timer, and a streak. Here's how they compare.
shot_alt: The BookWorm reading timer running for Shoe Dog by Phil Knight.

diff_body:
A daily goal, not only a yearly one. Pick pages or minutes a day and BookWorm helps you keep it: one reminder at lunchtime, a last call only when your streak is at risk, and nothing at all once you've read.

A real reading timer. Start a session and the clock runs on your Lock Screen and Dynamic Island, where you can pause and resume. Write a note mid-session, then log your page when you stop.

Quiet by design. No account, no feed, no recommendations. Just your books, your page and your streak, in a look you choose from four themes.
pick_title: When StoryGraph is the better choice
pick_body:
If you love digging into your reading stats, want recommendations based on mood and pace, or read with buddy reads and book clubs, StoryGraph is the stronger app for that. It also imports a Goodreads library in one go.

If what you want is to read a little every day and finish more of the books you start, that's what BookWorm is for.
a1: Yes, in hours and minutes. Listening counts toward the same daily goal as paper books and ebooks.
q2: Can I see my reading stats?
a2: Yes, more simply than StoryGraph: a calendar of reading days, your current and best streak, books finished this year, and a recap on the first of every month.
q3: Can I import my StoryGraph or Goodreads data?
a3: Not yet. You add the books you're reading now, which takes about a minute each with the built-in search.
a4: Yes, on iPhone and iPad, synced through your own iCloud account.
